newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Tan Chong stock suspended.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Tan Chong stock suspended.

text.p: Shares of Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd were suspended on Friday at the company's request, a statement from its merchant bankers said.

In a statement sent to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange late on Thursday, Commerce International Merchant Bankers Bhd said the Nissan car assembler is seeking a temporary stock suspension "pending a formal announcement". It did not give further details.
Officials at Tan Chong and Commerce International could not be reached for comment.

A report on Friday from research firm HLG Securities said there was speculation Tan Chong would announce a restructuring exercise involving the divestiture of its Singapore division, which consists of motor, property and overseas operations.
HLG said Tan Chong was also rumoured to be divesting its heavy equipment division and seeking to list its auto parts manufacturing firm on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
Jupiter Securities said in a report on Friday that investors were speculating on favourable results from the Malaysian auto industry's major players.

"More probable is that Tan Chong may actually win a contract to suppply heavy machineries to the Bakun project in Sarawak," the Jupiter report said, referring to the $5.5 billion Bakun hydro-electric dam in the East Malaysia state on Borneo island.
Officials at Ekran Bhd, the main contractor of the Bakun project, were not available for comment.
